call_points.text: Q1 margin hit by lower-margin domestic mix, near-zero-margin NTPC pilot and export dispatches pushed to Q2/Q3.
Domestic and product order booking fell 35.4% and 11.6% YoY; domestic enquiries declined broadly across industries.
U.S. facility to run at adequate but not high utilisation in FY27; product orders there would execute only in FY2028.
Receivables fell from Q4FY26, returning working capital to negative and raising cash.
Freight rates up 3-4x and vessel scarcity let clients defer export dispatches; freight is on clients' account, FOB.
Management expects quarter-to-quarter lumpiness to continue for a couple more quarters.
U.S. data centre enquiries growing as gas turbine lead times reach 4 years; conversion may come this year.
Small modular reactor work is at enquiry stage with long gestation.
No direct FY27 guidance; the 9% growth in closing order book is offered as the "minimum growth" to anticipate.
U.S. is now over 15% of the enquiry book, up from 1-2%, driven by data-centre combined cycle, biomass, pulp and geothermal.
Commodity inflation in copper, aluminium and steel is covered by long-term rate contracts and some customer pass-through; margins seen intact.
U.S. subsidiary had a profitable Q4 but a full-year FY26 loss of about ₹8 Cr; FY27 targeted positive or breakeven.
API turbines are a key growth and profit driver; management expects them to revert to a 10% plus share of order booking and revenue.
Export order inflow was flattish in FY26 as finalisations were delayed by geopolitical issues; management expects FY27 exports above domestic.
No API orders from the Middle East are in FY27 projections; higher oil prices have revived global API enquiries.
Data centres are well over half the enquiry book; long-term service contracts are booked only for the near-term executable year.

operating_notes.text: Product enquiry book is about 18 GW, nearly double FY25, with India at about 7 GW and the U.S. above 15% of the book.
The NTPC CO2 battery storage order runs at about 3% PBT margin and over two-thirds of it has been billed into revenue.
Aftermarket was 25% of Q4FY26 sales versus 33% a year earlier, and exports were 60% of Q4 revenue.
Order booking in Q1FY27 was ₹568 Cr, of which exports were 68% and aftermarket 39%; closing order book ₹2,180 Cr with exports 57% and aftermarket 29%.
About ₹175 Cr of the NTPC CO2-based energy storage order remained to execute at end-Q4, split roughly 40% in Q1, 40% in Q2 and the rest in Q3, at near-zero margin.
Bought-out content varies 30% to 70% of an order depending on customer scope; execution cycles run 7-8 months below 15 MW to about 18 months for 100 MW.

timeline.summary: On its 19 May 2026 Q4/FY26 call, Triveni Turbine reported FY26 revenue up 9% to ₹2,181 Cr with exports at 58% of sales, PAT down 3% on a ₹15.7 Cr wage-code charge, and a closing order book of ₹2,054 Cr, up 8%.
On 11 August 2026 Triveni Turbine's Q1FY27 call reported revenue up 19.2% to ₹4.43 bn but EBITDA margin down to 18% from 25.8%, with order booking up 6.1% to ₹5.68 bn on exports and aftermarket.
